tool_input.command: cd "$PWD" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --aggressive && git prune
tool_input.description: Run git cleanup: expire reflog, run aggressive garbage collection, and prune

tool_input.command:
git reflog expire --expire=now --all
git gc --aggressive
git prune
"Cleanup complete"
tool_input.description: Run git cleanup: expire reflog, run aggressive garbage collection, and prune

tool_input.command:
# Clear reflog
git reflog expire --expire=now --all 2>&1

# Prune unreachable objects
git prune 2>&1

# Check final git size
$gitSize = (Get-ChildItem -Path .\.git -Recurse -Force | Measure-Object -Property Length -Sum).Sum
"Final .git size: {0:N0} bytes ({1:N2} MB)" -f $gitSize, ($gitSize / 1MB)
tool_input.description: Clear reflog, prune objects, and check final size

result: Done. Git garbage collection completed successfully, reclaiming ~9 KB. The repository is quite small (0.05 MB total), so there wasn't much disk space to recover, but the cleanup removed loose and unreachable objects.
